title: Lead With Competence and Belonging Will Follow
author: Stuart Jr., Dave
summary: Stuart challenges the common start-of-year pedagogical sequence in which teachers spend significant time on icebreakers and community-building before beginning instruction, arguing that this sequence is backward. Belonging is most naturally produced by creating something worth belonging to—and the fastest route is demonstrating from Day One that the class will be led by a credible teacher, do valuable work, provide clear guidance for effective effort, and offer accessible definitions of success. The piece leans on the Five Key Beliefs pyramid’s design: Belonging sits at the top, emerging as a natural consequence of the other conditions rather than as their prerequisite. Stuart’s practical recommendation is to distribute get-to-know-you activities throughout the semester rather than concentrating them at the start, and to trust that a well-run class generates belonging as an inherent byproduct.
points: The common start-of-year icebreaker sequence is logically inverted: it tries to cultivate belonging in a class that has not yet been shown to be worth belonging to, which produces an artificial rather than earned sense of community.

Belonging is best built by creating something worth belonging to—a class with a credible teacher, valuable work, clear guidance for effort, and accessible success definitions—rather than by directly pursuing belonging through relationship activities.
The Five Key Beliefs pyramid encodes this insight visually: Belonging sits at the top, positioned as a natural consequence of the other four beliefs rather than as the foundation to establish first.

The practical recommendation is not to eliminate community-building activities but to distribute them across the semester, beginning the actual work of learning immediately and trusting that well-run instruction generates belonging as a byproduct.
quotes: There’s a common misconception amongst us teachers about how to develop Belonging in the classroom, and it’s this: at the start of the school year, you need to budget lots of time for things like icebreakers, get-to-know-you activities, and team-building exercises.

When you try to help your students develop a sense of Belonging to a class that hasn’t even started yet (because instead of beginning to teach the class, you’re focusing on cultivating belonging), you’re creating an unnatural thing. Instead, you want to create something worth belonging TO.
Rather than lots of icebreakers and get-to-know-yous, create enjoyable and productive learning experiences.
Who WOULDN’T want to believe they belong in a class led by a credible educator? Who WOULDN’T want to believe they belong in a class where the work is valuable?
The human heart is DRAWN to excellence, to value, to competence, to growth.
